info.title: sign-universal
info.description: Cross-platform code signing from Linux, macOS, or Windows with the private key held in Azure Trusted Signing, where it never leaves the HSM. Author-signs NuGet packages and Authenticode-signs Windows PE binaries. Fills the gap between `dotnet sign`, which supports Trusted Signing but only runs on Windows, and `dotnet nuget sign`, which runs anywhere but requires a local private key.

x-inspectra.cliParsedTitle: sign-universal - cross-platform code signing: NuGet packages and Windows PE
x-inspectra.cliParsedDescription: binaries, with the key held in Azure Trusted Signing.

commands.name: self-test
commands.description: Verify the remote-key -> SignedCms pipeline on this OS.

options.name: --hash
options.description: Digest algorithm: sha256 (default), sha384, or sha512.

options.name: --timestamper
options.description:
http://timestamp.digicert.com. Microsoft's
timestamp.acs.microsoft.com does not chain on a stock
Linux agent - see the README.

options.name: --no-timestamp
options.description:
Skip timestamping. Trusted Signing certificates expire in
days, and so will the signature.

options.name: --trust-signing-root
options.description:
Add the backend's root certificate to the current
user's trust store. Needed on Linux agents, where
signing otherwise fails with "Certificate chain
validation failed" - see the README.
Every format is timestamped by default.
`verify` reports the signer, whether the signature covers the file, and the
timestamp. It does not decide trust - use `signtool verify /pa` or
`dotnet nuget verify` for that.

options.name: --pfx
options.description:
A local PKCS#12 file. Its password
comes from SIGNUNIVERSAL_PFX_PASSWORD,
or --password-stdin, or --password
(which is visible in `ps` and shell
history - prefer the others).

options.description: Azure Trusted Signing. Also needs

options.name: --trusted-signing-account
options.description: and

options.name: --trusted-signing-certificate-profile
options.description:
Credentials come from AZURE_TENANT_ID / AZURE_CLIENT_ID /
AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET, as DefaultAzureCredential reads them.
